title.narrative: USAID Reducing conflict through Indigenous Women and Youth - CA Implementing Unit

description.narrative:
The USAID Reducing conflict through Indigenous Women and Youth Project, responds to the implementation in Honduras of this project by a consortium with CA (leading the Activity), the Organismo Cristiano de Desarrollo Integral de Honduras (OCDIH), and the Centro de Desarrollo Humano (CDH).
The project will be implemented, establishing 3 project pages in iPIMS, one for CA and each partner as follows:
1. USAID Reducing conflict through Indigenous Women and Youth - CA Implementing Unit. 2. USAID Reducing conflict through Indigenous Women and Youth - OCDIH. 3. USAID Reducing conflict through Indigenous Women and Youth - CDH
About the USAID Reducing conflict through Indigenous Women and Youth Project:
The project leverages the role of women and youth to support safe and secure environments, while building the capacity of traditional leadership structures and supporting dialogue to mitigate fragmentation within indigenous groups. It recognizes women and youth as rights holders with a fundamental stake in sustaining peace, while calling for an end to impunity in Honduras.
The project follows a P2P approach, bringing together representatives of indigenous groups who experience systemic, structural and physical violence at the local, regional and national level. The project focuses on creating inclusive space for indigenous women and youth to participate meaningfully, but recognizes in order to achieve this, there must be a safe and secure environment. ARC is informed by rigorous gender and age-sensitive analysis, understanding patriarchal norms, traditional gender roles, as well as the gendered impacts of conflict and NRM challenges. The design of the project focuses on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment, while cognizant of sensitivities and risks to women and youth.
The project will work directly with 37,968 people, representing the primary targets including those reached directly through communications and advocacy campaigns.
